observations.body: Paul and Barnabas separate over John Mark. After some days Paul said to Barnabas, “Let’s return now and visit our brothers in every city in which we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are doing.” He went through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the assemblies.

payload.posture: Read Acts 15:36–41 as one movement in Paul's story, keeping the passage's actions, setting, sequence, and limits visible.
payload.tension: The passage states paul and Barnabas separate over John Mark. After some days Paul said to Barnabas, “Let’s return now and visit our brothers in every city in which we proclaimed the word of the Lord, to see how they are doing.” He went through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the assemblies. It does not by itself supply every cause or later interpretation of this part of Paul's story.
